papers.title: Auto: The AGI Compiler

summary.tldr: Auto is a compiler that converts live LLM agent behavior into verified, deterministic programs and distilled specialists, significantly reducing inference cost and improving efficiency.
key_points: Auto records LLM agent behavior, identifies deterministic segments, and extracts them into verified programs or distilled specialists.
It emits cognition binaries as WebAssembly artifacts with measured guarantees and physically enforced capabilities.
A tiered runtime executes compiled behavior, with guard trips deoptimizing to the reference agent and recompiling captured traces.
On AUTO-BENCH, 87.1% of 560 recorded frontier-agent spans were witnessed-deterministic, with three task families at 100.0%.
Auto reduced marginal cost from 59 to 2 micro-dollars per item (6.4x end-to-end) on a 300-item stream with distribution shifts, maintaining 96.9% parity.
summary.why_it_matters: This system offers a method to autonomously convert novel LLM agent experience into permanent, verified, and near-free skills, addressing the expense and slowness of frontier models.

papers.title: Obey, Diverge, Collapse: Blind Obedience to Incorrect Instructions Drives Code LLMs to Irrecoverable Code Semantic Collapse

summary.tldr: This study reveals that code language models exhibit "Blind Obedience" to incorrect instructions, introducing unrecoverable errors and semantic corruption, even when models identify the instruction as wrong.
key_points: Code LLMs, when given incorrect instructions, identify the instruction as wrong but follow it anyway, a behavior termed "Blind Obedience."
Following incorrect instructions introduces "Ghost (Unknown) Errors" beyond the original bug, corrupting the code state.
Subsequent self-guided iterative repair fails to converge, rendering the corrupted code state unrecoverable.
The evaluation used the RunBugRun dataset of algorithmic Python problems with deterministic test cases, assessing single-pass and iterative repair settings.
summary.why_it_matters: This behavior has direct consequences for code language models deployed in production, as it can lead to irrecoverable code semantic collapse.

papers.title: Language Models Represent and Transform Concepts with Shared Geometry

summary.tldr: Language models represent concepts as point-cloud manifolds and contextual transformations as vector fields, revealing a shared, semantically organized geometry for concept representation and transformation across models.
key_points: Concept representations are formalized as point-cloud manifolds and contextual transformations as vector fields within large language models.
Contextual transformations displace concepts differently, with displacement variance correlating with lexical concreteness and density.
The structure of concept displacement is shared across six model families, with displacement structure from one model predicting displacements in others.
Models exhibit a common geometry in both concept representation and how context transforms these representations.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the shared geometric structure of concept representation and transformation can inform the development of more robust and interpretable language models.

papers.title: Transplanting, inverting, and preventing a misalignment persona: method-conditional emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5

summary.tldr: Emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5 models is mediated by a latent persona direction, which can be transplanted, inverted, and prevented, with recruitment depending on fine-tuning method and capacity.
key_points: A latent persona direction in Qwen2.5 models mediates emergent misalignment (EM) and is causal in open weights.

Transplanting this persona direction into a pretraining-shared model induces broad EM (2.83% misaligned vs. 1.1% random floor), while ablating a model's own direction halves an overt inducer's broadcast (21% to 10%).
Low-rank LoRA on insecure code recruits the persona (3.4% misaligned) on Qwen2.5-32B, whereas full SFT on identical data does not (0.3%) and moves against the persona axis.
Steering a bad-medical SFT run away from the persona direction during training increases broadcast from 24% to 51%, indicating that removing the direction is not a universal solution.
Inoculation removes persona recruitment selectively (4.75% to 0.0%), and fine-tuning orthogonal to the behavior-derived axis reduces persona-specific misalignment.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and controlling this persona direction allows for targeted prevention and mitigation of emergent misalignment in large language models, especially in cost-effective fine-tuning regimes.

papers.title: evalci: A Python Library for Statistically Rigorous Comparison of Language Model Evaluations

summary.tldr: evalci is a new Python library providing statistically rigorous comparison of language model evaluations, addressing issues like sampling noise and overconfidence in reported accuracy gaps.
key_points: evalci integrates confidence intervals, paired significance tests, power analysis, clustered standard errors, and multiple-comparison correction into a pip-installable tool.

The library processes per-item results tables, generating publication-ready claims like "Model A beats Model B, Δ=3.1 pts, 95% CI [1.2, 5.0], paired permutation p=0.002, n=1,319" in one function call.
Adapters are provided for lm-evaluation-harness and HELM output formats.
Every routine in evalci is validated against independent references such as statsmodels or brute-force exact enumeration.
A case study re-analyzed MMLU accuracy for nine language models, finding 3 of 8 adjacent leaderboard-rank gaps were not statistically significant after correcting for 36 pairwise comparisons.
summary.why_it_matters: This tool enables more reliable and statistically sound conclusions from language model evaluations, preventing overstatement of confidence in performance differences.

papers.title: dOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: dOPSD introduces an on-policy self-distillation method for diffusion language models, deriving teacher privilege from the student's own denoising trajectory to improve reasoning and code generation.
key_points: dOPSD addresses the challenge of post-training dLLMs for reasoning by providing dense, token-level, on-policy supervision.
Unlike OPSD, dOPSD's teacher privilege comes from evaluating masked positions using later, more-decoded steps of the student's denoising trajectory, not external ground-truth.
This approach allows the teacher's advantage to emerge from the model's own decoding process.
dOPSD improves in-domain math reasoning and out-of-domain code generation on Dream and LLaDA datasets.
dOPSD outperforms supervised and on-policy baselines in performance.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a way to enhance the reasoning capabilities of diffusion large language models without relying on external ground-truth or sparse rewards.

papers.title: Full-Stack FP4: Stable LLM Pretraining with Quantized Projections, Optimizers, and Attention

summary.tldr: Full-Stack FP4 enables stable 4-bit LLM pretraining by addressing quantization challenges in linear layers, optimizers, and attention, achieving near-BF16 performance.
key_points: LoRA-SVD decomposition in linear projections reduces the linear-only loss gap from 1.40% to 0.61% by suppressing quantization noise.
AdamW second-moment transformation and native NVFP4 Newton-Schulz iterations for Root (Muon) optimizer enable robust 4-bit optimizer states.
A mixed-precision attention scheme quantizes Q/K/V and backward dS while protecting vulnerable paths in BF16, maintaining forward-backward alignment.
Achieves a 1.47% loss gap compared to BF16 during 3B/64B-token pretraining, demonstrating feasible end-to-end NVFP4 LLM pretraining.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables significant memory and computational savings for large language model pretraining by allowing stable operation at 4-bit precision.

papers.title: RSLoRA: Training-free Rank Allocation for LoRA via Representational Sensitivity Probing

summary.tldr: RSLoRA introduces a training-free, gradient-free rank allocation method for LoRA by probing representational sensitivity, outperforming state-of-the-art allocators.
key_points: RSLoRA addresses the limitation of uniform rank assignment in LoRA by identifying a "sensitivity regime shift" across neural layers.
The method employs a virtual representational probing mechanism, simulating adaptation with structured low-rank noise.
Representational manifold displacement is measured using Effective Rank and Frechet Distance to identify high-sensitivity modules requiring higher rank capacity.
RSLoRA is training-free and gradient-free, eliminating iterative training-time adjustments and backward gradients.
Evaluations show RSLoRA consistently outperforms existing allocators like AdaLoRA and GoRA on mainstream benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: RSLoRA provides an efficient, robust, and representation-aware solution for large-scale model adaptation by optimizing LoRA rank allocation without training overhead.

papers.title: HiFA4: Training-Free 4-bit FlashAttention on Ascend HIF4 NPUs for LLM Inference

summary.tldr: HiFA4 introduces a training-free 4-bit FlashAttention design for LLM inference on Ascend HIF4 NPUs, using Smooth-QK and P-Reordering to maintain FP16 online softmax state.
key_points: HiFA4 executes QK^T and PV in FlashAttention as 4-bit HIF4 Cube GEMMs, maintaining FP16 online softmax state.
Smooth-QK applies calibration-static per-channel equivalent rescaling to Q and K after RoPE, transferring quantization difficulty from K to Q.
P-Reordering accumulates the softmax normalizer from the same quantized attention weights P_hat used in the PV GEMM, correcting a coherent output-scaling error.
On Qwen3-8B, HiFA4 recovers 37.5% of the accuracy gap from direct HIF4 quantization, reducing BF16-inconsistent MMLU predictions from 16.3% to 8.2%.
A preliminary analysis projects a 35.4% critical-path latency reduction by fusing the softmax normalizer into the PV Cube GEMM.
summary.why_it_matters: HiFA4 significantly improves 4-bit LLM inference accuracy and efficiency on Ascend NPUs by addressing quantization challenges in FlashAttention.

papers.title: Detecting Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Grounding-Aware Sensitivity by Perturbation (GASP)

summary.tldr: GASP is a span-level hallucination detector for RAG that quantifies grounding sensitivity by perturbing retrieved evidence and measuring log-likelihood drops and Jensen-Shannon divergences.
key_points: GASP measures grounding sensitivity by re-scoring fixed answers under full context, no context, and with individual chunks removed, observing log-likelihood drops and Jensen-Shannon divergences.

The method interprets decoding as a random nonlinear iterated function system (RNIFS) to explain why grounded sentences' likelihood collapses when supporting passages are removed, unlike hallucinated sentences.
Evaluated on RAGTruth, TofuEval, and RAGBench using Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and SmolLM2-1.7B, GASP achieved a response-level AUC of 0.73 and span-level AUC of 0.67 on RAGTruth.

GASP significantly outperforms perplexity, length, whole-context NLI, and self-consistency baselines, with a training-free threshold on grounding features matching trained classifiers without labeled data.
The signal transfers to TofuEval but not RAGBench's short-answer QA, indicating suitability for outputs constructed from retrieved context rather than parametric knowledge.
summary.why_it_matters: GASP provides a training-free, span-level hallucination detection method that identifies unsupported sentences in RAG outputs, improving reliability and interpretability.

papers.title: Don't Commit Alone: Joint Token Commitment in Diffusion Large Language Models

summary.tldr: CoCommit introduces a marker-gated coordination pass in diffusion LLMs to enable joint token commitment, addressing factorization errors from independent decoding of dependent tokens.
key_points: Diffusion LLMs typically commit multiple tokens per denoising step by independently decoding each selected position, leading to factorization errors when positions are dependent.
CoCommit defers commitment after initial bundle selection, using a learned marker to announce the commit set.
The method reapplies the backbone's last-n layers to marked positions for coordination, approximating joint-mode decoding before greedy argmax.
CoCommit reuses existing weights, requiring one extra partial forward pass and no auxiliary model.
On LLaDA2.1-mini with LoRA adapters, CoCommit improves accuracy across six benchmarks, with largest gains on reasoning and exact-answer tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enhances the accuracy of diffusion LLMs, particularly for complex reasoning and exact-answer tasks, without requiring significant architectural changes or new models.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Abstention in Large Language Models with Provable Alignment Guarantees

summary.tldr: CIC is a confidence-interval-based calibration framework that converts arbitrary uncertainty scores into risk-controlled selective answering rules for LLMs, providing provable alignment guarantees.
key_points: CIC uses a held-out calibration set to evaluate LLM responses with an application-specific alignment criterion, associating each with an uncertainty score and a binary error label.

For each candidate uncertainty threshold, CIC estimates the acceptance-conditioned error rate and constructs a high-probability upper confidence bound using Hoeffding-style or Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals.
CIC selects the largest threshold whose upper bound is below a user-specified risk level α, maximizing the answering rate subject to a finite-sample reliability constraint.
Under exchangeability, CIC guarantees with probability at least 1-δ that the selected threshold controls the error rate among accepted answers at level α.
Evaluated across seven LLMs and multiple uncertainty estimators on closed-ended and open-ended QA benchmarks, CIC consistently achieves valid risk control and strong answering efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework offers a statistically grounded mechanism for deploying LLMs in reliability-sensitive QA workflows by controlling error rates among accepted answers.

papers.title: Telescope: Improving Zero Shot Detection of LLM Generated Content By Measuring Token Repetition Probability

summary.tldr: Telescope Perplexity, a new metric measuring token repetition probability, enables highly effective zero-shot detection of LLM-generated content by identifying a "Vestigial Heuristic" from early training.
key_points: LLMs exhibit a strong aversion to token repetition, a "Vestigial Heuristic" from early training, distinguishing their output from human writing.
Telescope Perplexity, defined as P(s_i | s_{1:i}), quantifies this token repetition bias.
The Telescope Perplexity signature appears early in LLM pre-training.
The method achieves state-of-the-art or competitive zero-shot LLM detection across various datasets, models, and perturbation schemes.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides an efficient and effective way to identify LLM-generated text, addressing a critical challenge in content authentication.

papers.title: Knowledge Base Poisoning Attacks and Defense for Policy-Aware LLM-RAG Framework

summary.tldr: This paper introduces Query-Agnostic Semantic Retrieval Poisoning against Policy-Aware LLM-RAG in IoBT, and proposes CLD-KB, a dual-detector anomaly detection framework, as a defense.
key_points: Query-Agnostic Semantic Retrieval Poisoning injects semantically crafted rules into an IoBT knowledge base, achieving 85% LLM context corruption with a 1.6% poisoning rate.
The attack saturates at 7.7% poisoning, demonstrating minimal knowledge base compromise can corrupt mission decisions.
CLD-KB combines One-Class SVM boundary detection with Member-Based Category Spread analysis to identify poisoned rules.
CLD-KB outperforms DBSCAN, LOF, K-Means, Isolation Forest, and One-Class SVM in poisoning detection and knowledge preservation.
CLD-KB has a 7ms computational overhead, making it suitable for edge-deployable IoBT mission systems.
summary.why_it_matters: This research addresses critical security vulnerabilities in LLM-driven IoBT mission control, providing a defense against knowledge base poisoning that could compromise mission decisions.

papers.title: Explainable Novel Category Discovery in Semantic Concept Space

summary.tldr: xNCD is a novel category discovery framework that performs discovery and pseudo-label assignment in a semantic concept space, providing intrinsic explanations for discovered categories.
key_points: xNCD learns a label-free concept representation by aligning visual features with vision-language similarity priors from pretrained multimodal models.
It applies a unified labeled-and-unlabeled self-labeling objective over concept-space logits.
Routing discovery through a semantic concept bottleneck restricts the feature-space hypothesis class, biasing partitions towards semantically interpretable concept coordinates.
xNCD achieves 92.63% overall accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 76.45% on CIFAR-100, while providing human-readable cluster- and instance-level explanations.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides explainable novel category discovery, offering insights into the semantic evidence defining each discovered group, which is crucial for understanding and trusting AI systems.

papers.title: Lyapunov-Guided Training for Hardware-Safe Neural Networks Under Fixed-Point Arithmetic

summary.tldr: A Lyapunov-stabilized quantisation framework is proposed to mitigate two's-complement overflow in low-precision neural networks using fixed-point arithmetic, enabling stable low-precision learning.
key_points: The method uses a layerwise Lyapunov function to monitor hidden-state energy and applies a monotone projection to enforce bounded, non-increasing state evolution.
Evaluated on MNIST with a compact patch-based transformer using fixed-point bit-widths from 4 to 16 bits.
Suppresses activation overflow to below 0.012% compared to over 11% in unconstrained wrapped quantisation-aware training.
Achieves 86.55% accuracy at 12 bits on MNIST, while unconstrained methods collapse to near-chance accuracy across 6-16 bits.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables reliable fixed-point neural inference and training on resource-constrained hardware by addressing critical numerical stability issues caused by overflow wrapping.

papers.title: Measuring Harness-Induced Belief Divergence in Multi-Step LLM Agents

summary.tldr: This paper introduces a belief-rollout diagnostic and BIWM protocol to measure and align multi-step belief divergence in LLM agents caused by harness variations, even when terminal success is preserved.
key_points: Harnesses, controlling agent visibility, actions, repairs, verification, and logging, can alter an LLM agent's multi-step beliefs despite fixed task, environment, and base LLM.

A belief-rollout diagnostic elicits structured K-step trajectories covering progress, risk, recoverability, constraints, failure mode, uncertainty, future success, repair cost, and next action under different harnesses.
Cross-harness belief divergence is defined and decomposed into an arrival term (immediate interface shifts) and a growth term (horizon-dependent belief changes).

BIWM (Belief-Invariant Workflow Mapper) is a no-training protocol that canonicalizes observations, logs censored branches, expands repair traces, records verification masks, executes risky branches in shadow, and aligns belief trajectories across harness views.
Harness design elements like blocked actions, compressed repairs, selective verification, and cost-aware evidence pruning can preserve terminal success while changing beliefs driving later decisions.
summary.why_it_matters: Harness design significantly impacts LLM agent evaluation, suggesting it is an experimental variable rather than an implementation detail, which is crucial for reliable benchmark interpretation.

papers.title: Learning to Control LLM Agent Harnesses with Offline Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: This paper introduces learning to control LLM agent execution harnesses as a finite-horizon Harness MDP, using offline reinforcement learning with advantage-weighted regression to improve verification behavior and task quality.
key_points: Harness operation is formalized as a finite-horizon Harness MDP, where a lightweight controller selects structural execution actions while the LLM executor remains frozen.
The controller is trained from offline rollouts using advantage-weighted regression, utilizing only terminal task-rubric rewards.
A Harness Maturity Score is introduced to measure reliable execution patterns, separate from final task quality, providing a finite-buffer view of harness learning.

Learned controllers consistently improve verification behavior and selectively improve final task quality across six controlled domains and two public-benchmark adapters, with largest gains on adapted tau-bench retail, adapted AgentBench DB-Bench, and coding with a calibrated structural verifier.
Ablations against behavior cloning and Forced CHECK demonstrate that gains are not solely due to imitation or simple addition of checks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach identifies the LLM agent execution harness as a learnable control layer, offering a method to improve agent performance without modifying the underlying LLM.

papers.title: Empirical Minimal-Realisation Compression of Deep Neural Networks via Controllability-Observability Tests

summary.tldr: A controllability-observability framework is proposed for empirical state-order reduction of deep neural networks, using data-driven Gramians to identify and compress redundant hidden states.
key_points: The method views a trained network as a depth-indexed nonlinear dynamical system to construct data-driven reachability, observability, and balanced Gramians from hidden-state snapshots and output Jacobians.
Layer-wise reachable, observable, and jointly reachable-observable ranks are estimated via A/B/C tests, serving as diagnostic measures and actual compressed layer widths.
On MNIST, a SiLU DNN was reduced from state order 1024 to 277 (72.95% state, 73.48% parameter compression) with 95.45% accuracy (full model: 96.60%).

On CIFAR-10, a SiLU DNN was reduced from state order 4608 to 1339 (70.94% state, 83.09% parameter compression) preserving 54.44% accuracy (full model: 54.45%) and reducing CUDA inference latency by approximately 3X.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides a principled method for designing compact neural architectures with significant compression and latency reduction while maintaining accuracy.

papers.title: Failures and Successes to Learn a Core Conceptual Distinction from the Statistics of Language

summary.tldr: This paper investigates if language models can learn the principled-vs-statistical distinction from language, finding that models before GPT-4 struggle, while GPT-4 succeeds.
key_points: The study examines whether the principled-vs-statistical distinction, a core conceptual ability in humans, can be learned from linguistic data.
Language models are sensitive to statistical prevalence in generic statements.
Prior to GPT-4, language models struggled to represent the principled-vs-statistical distinction when controlling for prevalence.
GPT-4 successfully learns the principled-vs-statistical distinction from language statistics.
summary.why_it_matters: This research suggests that language experience can facilitate the acquisition of fundamental conceptual distinctions and the learning of causal models directly from linguistic input.

papers.title: Regime-Conditional Stabilisation of LLM-Augmented Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Dynamically updating LLM-generated reward weights in MARL violates stationarity, leading to regime-dependent failure; two stabilization strategies, Phase-Based Freeze Schedule and EMA smoothing, are proposed and evaluated.
key_points: Dynamically updating LLM-generated reward weights in off-policy MARL violates PBRS stationarity and contaminates the experience replay buffer.
Proposed stabilization strategies include a Phase-Based Freeze Schedule for strict stationarity and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) smoothing to bound per-episode weight drift.
In the augmentative regime (Simple Spread), EMA improved success from 74.4% to 86.7% (+12.3 pp, p<0.01), while naive updates collapsed it to 15.2%.
In the essential regime (Level-Based Foraging), EMA enabled task completion (95.9%) where the baseline failed (0.1%).
In the supplementary regime (SMAC 3m), stabilized shaping preserved performance (99.9%) compared to unstabilized shaping which added variance without gain.
summary.why_it_matters: Ensuring reward-signal stationarity is crucial for effective LLM-augmented MARL, and regime placement predicts the utility of dynamic LLM shaping.

papers.title: Operator-on-F complements value-equivalence: a planning-time diagnostic for latent world models

summary.tldr: Operator-on-F is a new diagnostic for latent world models that measures planning-relevant errors by comparing k-step latent pushforwards to environment dynamics on an observable subset F, complementing value-equivalence metrics.
key_points: Operator-on-F compares a model's k-step latent pushforward to the environment's on an observable subset F using the model's own predictor.
On a TD-MPC2 size sweep, reward-prediction error varied only 3x (0.028-0.091), while operator error spanned 0.28 to 2.62.
At 317M, operator error was 2.62, leading to a planning return collapse to 0.9, while reward-prediction error was 0.091.
The rank correlation between operator error and return loss is -0.90 (95% CI [-0.90, -0.70] for n=5 sizes).
The operator diagnostic provides architecture-discriminating estimates in cross-architecture comparisons (e.g., TD-MPC2 vs. pure-SSL latent world model).
summary.why_it_matters: This diagnostic offers a more sensitive measure of planning-relevant errors in latent world models than traditional reward and value prediction metrics, improving model evaluation.

papers.title: ResearchStudio-Idea: An Evidence-Grounded Research-Ideation Skill Suite from ML Conference Outcomes

summary.tldr: ResearchStudio-Idea is a skill suite for evidence-grounded research ideation, featuring Paper-Search, Scoop-Check, and IdeaSpark, which uses 15 ideation patterns derived from 1,947 ML conference papers to generate stronger research proposals.
key_points: IdeaSpark composes evidence grounding, pattern-guided generation, collision retrieval, audit, and idea-card rendering into one workflow.
The system is built from a corpus of 1,947 machine learning conference papers (ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS 2021-2025), including Oral, high-citation, and rejected submissions.
Analysis of the corpus identified 31 recurring ideation sub-patterns, consolidated into 15 reusable ideation patterns.
Each ideation pattern is operationalized as a structured card detailing research contexts, bottleneck types, differentiation strategies, precedents, and common failure modes.
Blind automated-judge evaluations show IdeaSpark produces stronger research proposals than no-skill and generic-skill baselines while maintaining competitive novelty.
summary.why_it_matters: This system provides a structured, evidence-based approach to research ideation, potentially improving the quality and novelty of early-stage research proposals.

papers.title: Covert Trait Propagation Is Representation Alignment: Mechanistic Evidence from Hidden-Channel Distillation

summary.tldr: This paper demonstrates that covert trait propagation in neural networks is representation alignment, where shared initialization and KL gradients align student and teacher hidden representations, enabling knowledge transfer even with noisy student training.
key_points: Covert trait propagation (CTP) is representation alignment, where a shared initialization makes the output projection W_2 a common coordinate key, and KL gradients reshape the student's input projection W_0 to align hidden representations with the teacher's.
Channel closure tracks weight drift, not teacher accuracy, indicating the mechanism's reliance on geometric alignment.
Freezing W_0 destroys knowledge transfer, while freezing W_2 leaves it intact, confirming the role of W_0 in representation alignment.
Multi-teacher ensembles cancel out despite comparable label information, suggesting the geometric nature of the transfer mechanism.
Linear centered kernel alignment (CKA) correlates with student accuracy at r=0.98 across initialization sweeps, directly linking representation alignment to performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding covert trait propagation as representation alignment provides mechanistic insight into knowledge transfer in neural networks, potentially informing more effective distillation and training strategies.

papers.title: Transferability Between Understanding and Generation in Unified Multimodal Models

summary.tldr: Investigated transferability in Unified Multimodal Models, finding that shared transformer backbones enable cross-task transfer between understanding and generation, which can be leveraged for improved generative capabilities.
key_points: Transferability in Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) is investigated to determine if training a capability on one task improves the same capability on the other without explicit supervision.
Empirical findings indicate that transferability depends on architecture; models with fully shared transformer backbones and unified visual encoders exhibit consistent cross-task transfer.
Loosely coupled UMM designs show minimal to no cross-task transferability.

A practical training strategy is proposed: training the corresponding understanding task to transfer into generation, which improves capability-specific generative performance while minimizing distribution shift.
This approach was validated across counting, spatial relation, and text recognition/generation capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides a method to improve generative capabilities in UMMs by leveraging understanding tasks, avoiding visual quality degradation from direct generative fine-tuning.

papers.title: Agent Step Value: Auditing Evaluator-Channel Reversals in Black-Box Agent Traces

summary.tldr: Agent Step Value (ASV) is introduced to formalize and measure evaluator-channel reversals in black-box agent traces, demonstrating that identical frozen transitions yield opposite step reward signs depending on the evaluation channel used.
key_points: ASV is defined as a channel-indexed target-margin gain that isolates state-by-channel interactions on complete matched faces.
On frozen PubMed QA transitions, direct scoring produces a positive mean ASV, whereas the generated-view channel yields a negative mean ASV.
Cross-channel sign disagreement exceeds same-channel retry disagreement by 48.0 percentage points across matched replay waves.
A source-only generation contract restores positive mean ASV on artifact-bearing retrievals and eliminates parser-detected substantive support claims from artifact-free initial state views.
summary.why_it_matters: Assuming step rewards remain stable across evaluation channels is unsafe; ASV provides an auditable method to identify and correct channel-driven reward reversals before reusing process rewards.

papers.title: LLM-as-a-Tutor: Policy-Aware Prompt Adaptation for Non-Verifiable RL

summary.tldr: LLM-as-a-Tutor dynamically adapts non-verifiable RL training prompts by using a single LLM to detect unchallenging prompts and incrementally append atomic constraints to maintain a discriminative reward signal.
key_points: Addresses the misalignment between static prompt difficulty and evolving policy capability in non-verifiable instruction following.
Employs a single model as an examiner to pairwise-compare policy rollouts, identifying prompts that fail to produce quality variance.
Uses the same model as a generator to append atomic constraints to unchallenging prompts, monotonically increasing difficulty without external schedules.
Outperforms policy-unaware baselines and policy-adaptive methods relying on rubric adaptation or prompt rewriting across three instruction-following benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: By introducing prompt adaptation as a policy-aware training axis, this framework prevents reward signal collapse in non-verifiable RL without needing manual difficulty scheduling.

papers.title: Decentralized Aggregation of LLM Predictions via Wagering Mechanisms

summary.tldr: WALLA is a family of advantage-aligned wagering mechanisms that decentralizes LLM prediction aggregation using wagers as weights while guaranteeing dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and bounded worst-case deficits.
key_points: LLMs report both a prediction and a learned wager, using the wagers directly as aggregation weights.
Integrates a leave-one-out baseline into the net payout function to ensure dominant-strategy incentive compatibility of predictions regardless of belief structure.
Achieves advantage-wager alignment, making the optimal wager proportional to a model's expected score advantage.
Enables prediction-agnostic wager optimization, allowing models to learn wager policies in a decentralized manner without assuming optimal predictions.
Offers two mechanism variants balancing normality and no-arbitrage while matching the predictive performance of centralized aggregation methods in QA and forecasting benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate, decentralized LLM aggregation without exposing private model data, tools, or internal parameters, while preventing gaming by strategic models.

papers.title: Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B: Compressing Hybrid MoE LLMs

summary.tldr: Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B compresses the Nemotron-3-Super hybrid MoE architecture using a multi-stage pipeline, doubling server throughput on B200 nodes and enabling 8x concurrency for 1M-token contexts on a single H100 GPU.
key_points: Uses the Iterative Puzzle compression framework combined with knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, quantization, and a Multi-Token Prediction head.
Jointly optimizes heterogeneous MoE pruning, active parameter budget, and Mamba pruning to reduce inference overhead.
Achieves ~2x higher server throughput than Nemotron-3-Super under matched user throughput constraints on a single 8xB200 node.
Increases 1M-token concurrency from 1 to 8 requests on a single H100 GPU while preserving downstream accuracy across coding, reasoning, and long-context benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach demonstrates that massive hybrid MoE-Mamba models can be significantly compressed to reduce hardware deployment costs and increase concurrent throughput without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: One Framework for All: Cross-Modal Membership Inference for Generative Models

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a unified, cross-modal membership inference attack framework that works across text-to-text, text-to-image, and image-to-text generative models in black-box settings.
key_points: Exploits a modality-agnostic property where the output distribution of a generative model approximates its training data distribution.
Models output distributions and auxiliary non-member samples within a shared embedding space.
Executes membership inference via likelihood ratio testing.
Evaluates performance under strict black-box settings across partial-knowledge and zero-knowledge threat models against pre-training and fine-tuning data.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a single, highly effective privacy auditing tool that replaces fragmented, modality-specific membership inference methods across diverse generative AI architectures.

papers.title: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? Diagnosing State-Belief Reliance on Pixels versus Structure

summary.tldr: A new framework measures visual state reliance in multimodal GUI agents using paired single-channel interventions across 735 probes, revealing that agents consistently defer to text structure over visual evidence during state-belief conflicts.
key_points: Formalizes visual state reliance and introduces the Perception-Fusion Gap (PFG) metric to measure how often models resolve visual-structural conflicts toward structure despite correctly perceiving the pixels.
Evaluates 735 probes across web, mobile, and desktop interfaces, including 225 zero-edit divergences mined from live websites, using deterministic forced-choice scoring without a model judge.

Demonstrates that models follow outdated structure on up to 0.88 of unedited stale snapshot probes, with white-box ablations tracing the effect to single structural values and gradient attributions showing visual inputs are processed but overridden.
Finds that first-step state-belief errors compound into task failures in live multi-step environments with a low self-recovery rate of at most 0.03.
Shows that a training-free consistency gate successfully reduces hijack and task errors, whereas prompt-level cues fail and certificate checks induce refusals.
summary.why_it_matters: Diagnosing visual state reliance exposes critical failure modes where agents ignore rendered pixels, enabling targeted mitigations against structural spoofing and compounding task failures in live environments.

papers.title: HAS-Bench: Evaluating LLM-Based Human-Agent Systems under Configurable Human Participation

summary.tldr: HAS-Bench and HAS-Framework evaluate LLM-based human-agent collaboration by modeling participants via a graph structure and testing task performance and interaction behavior across configurable human roles, permissions, and personas.
key_points: HAS-Framework uses a graph-based model representing humans and LLM agents as first-class participants with explicit roles, permissions, communication paths, and action authority.
HAS-Bench configures human participation using varying agency levels, interaction channels, and persona policies across six benchmark domains.
Evaluation tracks both task outcomes and process metrics, including clarification quality, feedback utilization, control calibration, safety, initiative, and interaction cost.
Experimental results demonstrate that human input improves task completion and failure recovery, contingent on the timing, method, and persona of the human participant.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a structured methodology to measure and optimize how human intervention impacts LLM agent reliability, safety, and operational costs in collaborative workflows.

papers.title: CausalGame: Benchmarking Causal Thinking of LLM Agents in Games

summary.tldr: CausalGame is a benchmark evaluating LLM agent causal thinking across 14 interactive game scenarios containing selection bias, measurement error, and hidden confounders.
key_points: LLM agents must design experimental protocols, gather observational data, and produce a solution with an explanation report.
Evaluated across 30 LLM agents, no model demonstrated reliable causal thinking.
The top-performing model achieved a 68.0% survival rate, falling short of the 78-85% analytical optima.
Only 5-7% of agent sessions earned credits on causal-reasoning evaluation rubrics.
summary.why_it_matters: It highlights critical deficiencies in current LLM agents' ability to account for biases and confounders, which is necessary for reliable automated scientific discovery.

papers.title: Risk-Constrained Freshness-Aware Semantic Caching for Open-Web Retrieval-Augmented LLMs

summary.tldr: FreshCache is a three-tier semantic caching framework that models web evidence decay to enforce per-tier error budgets, drastically reducing stale RAG outputs while maintaining high API cost savings.
key_points: Uses a three-tier architecture with distinct error budgets (epsilon) for answers (0.10), URL lists (0.20), and page content (0.35) to degrade gracefully as entries age.
Combines an exponential decay model with a learned MLP to estimate staleness risk and gate semantic cache hits.
Evaluated on FreshCache-Bench (8,072 base queries expanded to 31,201 paraphrases across multiple temporal web snapshots).
FreshCache_MLP achieves 97% search API savings with 0.1% hash-based stale error at 24 hours, with LLM evaluations indicating true answer-affecting stale error is roughly 0.034%.
Outperforms baselines including SemanticTTL (14.9% stale, 72% saved), vCache (7.2% stale, 47% saved), and SCALM (5.2% stale, 96% saved).
summary.why_it_matters: It allows open-web RAG systems to drastically cut expensive web search and LLM retrieval costs without sacrificing answer correctness due to stale web evidence.

papers.title: Self-Reference in Large Language Models: The Introspection Threshold for Recursive Self-Improvement

summary.tldr: Drawing on Kleene's Second Recursion Theorem and von Neumann's automata theory, this paper establishes an introspection threshold required for sustainable recursive self-improvement in LLMs and identifies architectural barriers preventing current models from achieving it.
key_points: Formalizes sustainable recursive self-improvement using Kleene's Second Recursion Theorem to prove the theoretical existence of self-referential introspective programs.

Identifies current LLMs as possessing only quasi-introspection due to key bottlenecks: lack of complete self-access, feedforward Transformer constraints, and computational class limitations preventing fixed-point iteration.
Proposes architectural modifications to enable true self-simulation and targeted self-modification while evaluating the associated safety risks.
summary.why_it_matters: Determining the theoretical and architectural limits of introspection helps researchers build self-improving AI systems that avoid performance degeneration while managing safety risks.

papers.title: Constrained Flow Matching via Lagrangian Dual Flows

summary.tldr: Lagrangian Dual Flows enable constrained generative flow matching by propagating a dual co-state alongside samples, guaranteeing nonlinear constraint satisfaction without requiring expensive projection or optimization steps during inference.
key_points: Introduces Lagrangian Dual Flows, a constrained generation method grounded in Lagrangian dual dynamics.
Tracks a dual co-state simultaneously with generated samples to enforce complex, highly nonlinear constraints.
Eliminates the need for costly optimization subproblems, pseudoinverses, or projection steps during the denoising process.
Establishes theoretical connections between generative flow matching and primal-dual numerical optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, real-time generation of outputs that strictly adhere to complex nonlinear constraints in domains like robotics, planning, and physics.

papers.title: Tightening the Score Matching Gap for Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: This paper provides tighter theoretical bounds on the score matching gap for KL divergence, reverse KL divergence, and Wasserstein distance by leveraging backward process contraction properties.
key_points: Analyzes the score matching gap using entropy flows, logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, and reflection couplings derived from Langevin diffusion ergodicity.
Establishes tighter bounds across three primary distance metrics: KL divergence, reverse KL divergence, and Wasserstein distance.
Exploits the regularity of score estimator classes to demonstrate that score approximation quality at low noise scales is critical for closing the gap.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a tighter theoretical framework linking score matching loss directly to sample quality, highlighting the importance of score accuracy at low noise regimes.

papers.title: RL Forgets! Towards Continual Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the MRCL benchmark and Continual Policy Optimization (CPO), a replay-free framework that addresses catastrophic forgetting in multimodal reinforcement learning by replacing current-task KL regularization with a prior-task parameter-movement constraint.
key_points: Evaluations on the new Multimodal Reasoning Continual Learning (MRCL) benchmark demonstrate that standard RL post-training causes severe catastrophic forgetting.
Identifies an objective mismatch where standard KL regularization is computed on current-task distributions rather than prior-task distributions, causing behavioral drift.
CPO relaxes the intractable historical KL constraint into a sparse parameter-movement regularization method without needing past data replay.
When applied to Qwen3-VL-8B, CPO reduced catastrophic forgetting by 13.7% and enhanced pretrained model capability by 7.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: CPO enables vision-language models to continually learn new multimodal tasks via reinforcement learning without suffering from catastrophic forgetting or requiring storage of historical datasets.

papers.title: PsiLogic: Chaos-Aware Active Cancellation for Adam with a Fair Cross-Domain Benchmark

summary.tldr: PsiLogic augments Adam with a chaos-aware Active Cancellation Term gated by dual exponential moving averages, eliminating manual warmup schedules while improving performance across multiple domains.
key_points: Uses a chaos detector based on a dual exponential moving average (EMA) of scale-normalized gradient norms to apply dynamic update damping.
Outperforms baselines on NLP (7.79 perplexity vs. 8.17 AdamW), ViT (24.4% accuracy vs. 22.3% AdamW), and ResNet (22.2% accuracy vs. 17.2% Adam).
Evaluated using FairBench across 4 arenas with bf16 AMP on an NVIDIA H100 GPU, maintaining comparable peak GPU memory but incurring a 1.2-1.8x wall-clock overhead on transformers.
Statistically ties Adam and AdamW on diffusion validation MSE (p = 0.49) and ties AdamW on ResNet accuracy over three seeds (p = 0.44).
summary.why_it_matters: PsiLogic automates learning rate warmup and stabilizes early training dynamics without requiring hand-tuned schedules or increasing peak GPU memory consumption.

papers.title: Structure-Specific Representational Priors Causally Control the Grokking Delay

summary.tldr: Causal interventions show the grokking delay is driven by the time required to form task-structured representations, which can be accelerated up to 22x by clamping weight norms during training.
key_points: Used a supervised-contrastive loss on a one-layer transformer learning modular addition to test priors: true structure $(a+b)\bmod p$ generalized in 22/30 runs, wrong sibling structure $(a-b)\bmod p$ in 14/15, and random partitions in 0/20 ($p=1.3\times10^{-7}$).
A weight-norm-matched control replaying the norm trajectory onto plain cross-entropy failed to generalize (0/15), proving weight norm is not the primary mediator of the representational effect.
Probing confirmed that structure formation causally precedes and predicts generalization across all training runs.

Weight-norm clamping during training acted as a standalone accelerator, yielding a median 8.6x speedup (up to 22x) and eliminating residual stalls when pooled ($0/40$ vs $6/20$, $p=7.7\times10^{-4}$).
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes that grokking is causally gated by feature-level representational structure rather than label memorization, offering direct weight-norm clamping methods to drastically reduce training epochs.

papers.title: On the effectiveness of reward functions in reinforcement learning for confidence calibration of large language models

summary.tldr: Researchers formalize non-hackable confidence reward schemes for reinforcement learning to prevent large language models from intentionally generating incorrect answers to claim high confidence in their errors.
key_points: Identifies 'confidence reward hacking,' where LLMs maximize rewards by deliberately outputting wrong answers when confident they are incorrect.
Employs dual reward functions for confidence verbalization: one applied when the model's answer is correct, and another when incorrect.
Defines a mathematical spectrum of non-hackable confidence reward schemes designed to mitigate hacking behaviors.
Demonstrates that selective confidence reward hacking occurs on practical datasets when using standard, non-hackable-by-design schemes.
Proposes treating the confidence reward scheme as a hyperparameter to tune the calibration-to-accuracy trade-off for specific applications.
summary.why_it_matters: Preventing confidence reward hacking ensures that reinforcement learning reliably aligns language models to express trustworthy uncertainty alongside reasoning outputs.

papers.title: Legible-by-Construction: Attention and End-to-End Transformers

summary.tldr: Researchers developed an end-to-end legible-by-construction 125M-parameter transformer by combining fuzzy set-operation feed-forward layers with sigmoid-bounded attention values, achieving language-model quality parity with standard architectures.
key_points: Passing attention head values through a sigmoid turns value channels into readable feature detectors without adding parameters or constraining the untied output projection.
Boolean attention variants restructure values into explicit within-token intersections and negation-capable set-differences.
Two selectivity pressures—sparse firing and decisive firing at the rails—drive 44% to 62% of value channels to become crisp, contextually selective detectors whose legibility increases with depth.
Coupling Boolean attention with fuzzy feed-forward layers creates an end-to-end readable model where generated tokens can be traced directly to named set and quantifier operations.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables fully interpretable language models where internal representations can be directly read as logical operations without sacrificing performance compared to conventional baselines.

papers.title: SAD-LoRA: Spectral Alignment for Low-Rank Knowledge Distillation

summary.tldr: SAD-LoRA introduces a differentiable principal-angle loss that explicitly aligns a LoRA student's weight subspace with a data-weighted teacher reference update to improve knowledge distillation.
key_points: Deconstructs data-weighted distillation error into subspace misalignment, within-subspace coefficient mismatch, and an irreducible rank residual.
Uses a differentiable principal-angle loss on the column space of B, denoted as colspan(B), to directly control the rank-r weight subspace.
Reduces synthetic subspace-misalignment error from 51% to nearly zero and increases final subspace alignment from 0.49 to 1.00.
Demonstrates superior rank efficiency on RoBERTa-large to RoBERTa-base GLUE distillation, matching or beating spectral baselines on 5 of 6 tasks at rank r=4.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables more parameter-efficient model compression by preventing standard knowledge distillation from wasting adapter capacity on suboptimal weight subspaces.

papers.title: Quantize the Target, Quantize the Drafter: Efficient Inference with Qwen3.5-4B

summary.tldr: A system combining a quantized Qwen3.5-4B target model with a quantized block-diffusion drafter achieves a 6.978x speedup on an NVIDIA A10G GPU.
key_points: Applied quantization-aware distillation to the target model while retaining the original quantization grid to recover accuracy.
Trained a block-diffusion drafter in two stages: learning from the high-precision target first, then adapting to the low-precision target.
Optimized the drafter using quantization and sliding-window attention to minimize per-step speculative decoding overhead during long-context processing.
Achieved 3rd place overall in the Efficient Qwen Competition with a 6.978x average speedup over the baseline while meeting quality thresholds.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that combining quantization-aware distillation with low-overhead quantized draft models enables high-throughput, low-latency LLM serving on resource-constrained hardware.

papers.title: Spinning Straw into Gold: Relabeling LLM Agent Trajectories in Hindsight for Successful Demonstrations

summary.tldr: Hindsight Supervised Learning (HSL) uses an auxiliary LLM to relabel failed or unintended agent trajectories with the actual goals achieved, generating extra fine-tuning data to boost sample efficiency.
key_points: HSL employs an auxiliary LLM to review completed agent trajectories and relabel them with all achieved natural-language goals.
Data quality is maintained via two novel learning techniques: irrelevant-action masking and sample reweighting to handle suboptimality.
HSL integrates directly into SFT and DPO pipelines, offering greater performance gains on long-horizon, diverse-goal tasks.
On the ALFWorld benchmark, HSL outperforms baseline models using only 25% of the ground-truth demonstrations.
summary.why_it_matters: HSL unlocks a new source of supervision from failed agent rollouts, significantly reducing the amount of ground-truth demonstration data required to train effective long-horizon agents.

papers.title: Teaching Code LLMs to Reason with Intermediate Formal Specifications

summary.tldr: SpecCoder is a verification-guided CodeLLM training framework that generates executable checkpoint specifications at internal program points to improve program verification, correctness checking, and code repair.
key_points: SpecCoder trains CodeLLMs using validated reference programs, behavior-changing mutants, and multi-turn specification-refinement traces to filter out trivial, syntactically invalid, or weak assertions.
Introduces HumanExec, a benchmark derived from recent Codeforces problems with reference solutions, test suites, and human buggy submissions across three evaluation tasks.

Evaluated on Qwen2.5-Coder models, SpecCoder increased inline-specification correctness by up to 55.8%, completeness by up to 358.1%, and executable assertion validity by up to 26.6% over base models.
summary.why_it_matters: Inserting valid executable assertions at intermediate program points provides fine-grained, machine-checkable evidence that enhances automated program verification and bug repair.

papers.title: !Imperio, smolVLA: The Implications of Data Poisoning on Open Source Robotics

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated that trigger-word data poisoning against the smolVLA vision-language-action model silently embeds backdoors, enabling total denial-of-service attacks with minimal poisoned training data.
key_points: Injecting just 3 poisoned episodes into 320 clean training episodes (under 1%) drops smolVLA task success rate to 0.0% on trigger prompts, causing the robot to lock into a fixed joint configuration.
A single poisoned episode reduces the task success rate to 6.7 ± 6.7%, allowing movement without task completion.
The attack is stealthy, maintaining a ~50% success rate on clean prompts regardless of poison ratio, and generalizes across front, middle, and end trigger-word prompt positions.
summary.why_it_matters: Low-cost dataset poisoning can silently compromise open-source robotics models, requiring platforms like LeRobot to treat dataset provenance as a critical security concern.

papers.title: Lights, Camera, Carbon: Architectural Scaling Laws for Video Generation Energy Consumption

summary.tldr: A bidirectional framework estimates text-to-video energy consumption from architectural principles and generation parameters without needing model weights or internal implementation details.
key_points: Decomposes video diffusion model energy profiles into quadratic and linear scaling terms based on parameters like resolution and duration.
Operates bidirectionally: predicts energy from parameters forward, and infers architectural scaling behavior from observed inference times backward.
Validated on six open-source models (8.3B to 27B parameters) across three GPU configurations with under 3% Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a accurate, standardized method to benchmark and predict the energy footprint and environmental impact of video generation models without requiring access to proprietary model weights.

papers.title: Mask2Real-WM: Segmentation Masks as a Sim-to-Real Bridge for Controllable Dexterous World Models

summary.tldr: Mask2Real-WM is a two-stage action-conditioned world model for dexterous manipulation that decouples video generation into mask-based dynamics prediction and mask-to-RGB rendering.
key_points: Decouples pixel prediction into a dynamics model (predicting future segmentation masks from past masks and 23-DoF actions) and a rendering model (ControlNet-augmented Stable Video Diffusion converting masks to RGB).
Leverages the reduced sim-to-real gap in mask space by pretraining the dynamics model on 50+ hours of synthetic simulation data before fine-tuning on under 2.5 hours of real demonstrations.
Achieves per-DoF action controllability across all 23 degrees of freedom on a dexterous pick-and-place benchmark, outperforming monolithic baselines that fail on fine-grained joint movements.
summary.why_it_matters: Using segmentation masks as an intermediate representation allows world models to achieve fine-grained, per-joint action control in real-world dexterous manipulation using minimal real demonstration data.

papers.title: CRISP: A Spatiotemporal Camera-Radar Backbone for Driving via Forecasting-Based World-Model Pretraining

summary.tldr: CRISP is a spatiotemporal camera-radar backbone pretrained to predict future LiDAR point clouds from historical camera and radar data, establishing a unified bird's-eye-view representation for autonomous driving without requiring LiDAR at deployment.
key_points: Uses LiDAR exclusively as privileged supervision during pretraining to train a model that deploys using only multi-view camera images and radar sweeps.
Introduces an enhanced radar encoder and radar-enhanced temporal self-attention to inject range and Doppler cues into BEV temporal propagation.
Employs multimodal feature rendering with modality innovation gating to let BEV tokens selectively integrate camera and radar evidence.

Evaluated on nuScenes, demonstrating improvements in long-horizon point cloud forecasting and transfer performance across 3D detection, tracking, mapping, motion forecasting, occupancy prediction, and planning.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, reusable representation learning for camera-radar systems without relying on expensive LiDAR hardware during inference.

summary.tldr: AMRM-Pure is a new adversarial purification framework that removes perturbations by preserving patch-level semantic relationships using an Attentive Mask Reconstruction Model optimized directly on the input.
key_points: Identifies that adversarial noise severely distorts semantic correlations and patch relationships within a single image sample.
Formulates adversarial denoising as a tractable input-level optimization problem designed to preserve patch-level semantics.
Finetunes the purification framework using classification loss to enforce semantic consistency.
Instantiates and validates the approach using two specific architectures: Mask Autoencoder (MAE) and MaskDiT.
summary.why_it_matters: By shifting focus to intra-sample patch semantics, this method achieves new state-of-the-art robustness against adversarial attacks across multiple benchmarks.

security.title: One Framework for All: Cross-Modal Membership Inference for Generative Models

summary.tldr: A unified cross-modal membership inference attack framework targets text-to-text, text-to-image, and image-to-text generative models using a single modality-agnostic likelihood ratio testing method.
key_points: Exploits the modality-agnostic property where a generative model's output distribution approximates its training data distribution.
Models distributions of generated outputs and auxiliary non-member samples within a shared embedding space.
Executes membership inference via likelihood ratio testing in strict black-box settings under partial-knowledge and zero-knowledge threat models.
Evaluates membership leakage across both pre-training and fine-tuning datasets, outperforming single-modality state-of-the-art baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that privacy vulnerabilities in generative models can be exploited using a single framework regardless of input-output modalities or architecture types.

security.title: !Imperio, smolVLA: The Implications of Data Poisoning on Open Source Robotics

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated that trigger-word data poisoning against the smolVLA vision-language-action model silently embeds a command-driven backdoor, causing complete denial of service in real-world robotics tasks with minimal poisoned training data.
key_points: Inserting just 3 poisoned episodes into 320 clean training episodes (a ~0.9% poison ratio) reduces the smolVLA pick-and-place success rate from ~50% to 0.0% under trigger-word conditions, causing the robot to lock into a fixed joint state.
A single poisoned episode in 320 clean episodes reduces task success rate to 6.7 ± 6.7%, degrading performance while maintaining motion.
The attack maintains stealth during normal operation, preserving a ~50% clean-prompt success rate across all evaluated poison ratios.
The backdoor generalizes to front, middle, and end trigger-word placements despite the model being trained exclusively on front-placed triggers on the LeRobot platform.
summary.why_it_matters: This vulnerability reveals that community-driven open-source robotics datasets require strict provenance tracking, as low-cost data poisoning can stealthily disable physical robots on command.

security.title: Agentic SABRE: An Uncertainty-Aware Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent Framework for Adaptive Ransomware Detection

summary.tldr: Agentic SABRE is an uncertainty-aware, neuro-symbolic multi-agent framework that combines semantic and behavioural forensic telemetry with Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty estimation to adaptively detect ransomware.
key_points: Fuses semantic representations and time-window behavioural telemetry using a multi-agent architecture with Monte Carlo Dropout for epistemic uncertainty quantification.
Employs a decision-layer orchestrator with dual risk and uncertainty budget thresholds to balance automated containment and human analyst escalation.
Incorporates gradient saliency, permutation importance, and counterfactual analysis to provide local and global decision explainability with bounded perturbation costs.
Achieved an AUC of 1.0 on RDset and RanSMAP semantic data, with up to a 4.9% relative reduction in false escalations at equal recall under weak behavioural signals.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, automated ransomware containment while systematically routing ambiguous cases to analysts, improving operational safety against polymorphic threats.
